2.alt: An open illustrated book sits beside a round stamp reading Review 1.2.0 and a small magnifying glass.

4.text:
A detective looks for clues.
Spot a clue.
Say what you notice.
Turn the page to check.
4.subtext: A clue is something you notice that helps you look again.

5.text:
Mira is in her room.

Can you spot five things?
5.subtext: Look carefully. The next page will name the objects.
5.alt: A recognisable bedroom shows Mira and Pip with a bed and pillow, four-pane window, bookshelf with coloured books, standing lamp, striped rug, open toy box and yellow bell. No object names are shown yet.

6.text:
You found Mira's room!

Now follow each label to its object.
6.subtext: Can you find one more object than the labels name?
6.alt: The same bedroom returns with clear arrow labels naming MIRA, PIP, BED, WINDOW, BOOKS, LAMP, RUG, BOX and BELL. A ticket reads BOOK CODE ROOMSTAR.

8.alt: The open toy box reveal labels MIRA LOOKING, BOX, PIP WATCHING, TOY OUTSIDE and EMPTY INSIDE.

9.text:
A container is something that can hold things, like this box.

EMPTY tells us what is missing from inside it.
9.subtext: The container can still be here.
9.alt: Pip places the first gold star on the map beside a recognisable open toy box. A ticket reads BOOK CODE BOXCLUE.

11.alt: A recognisable yellow hand bell stands still beside Mira and Pip. Written labels read MIRA LISTENING, PIP WAITING and BELL STAYED STILL. A ticket reads BOOK CODE QUIETWINGS.

12.alt: A familiar blank-paper emoji, purple feather, magnifying glass and pencil are shown without names for the child to spot.

13.text:
The card was here.
A pencil was here.
A feather and a magnifying glass were here.
13.alt: The blank-card reveal labels CARD, PENCIL, PIP'S FEATHER and MAGNIFYING GLASS. A ticket reads BOOK CODE BLANKEDGE.

16.text:
Mira put the toys behind a curtain.
Part of each toy was hidden.

Did the room become nothing?
16.subtext: Spot what stayed in the picture.

17.text:
Part of each toy was hidden.
The curtain was here.
Mira and Pip were still playing.
17.subtext: A view is what we can see from one place. Hidden from this view is not gone.
17.alt: A recognisable purple curtain and partly visible teddy and box are labelled CURTAIN and TOYS PARTLY HIDDEN. Written labels also name MIRA and PIP. A ticket reads BOOK CODE CURTAINMAP.

19.text:
Door A holds out a card.
Door B holds out no card.

Which door gives Mira something to look at?
19.subtext: Something shown for us to look at is called an example.
19.alt: Labelled doors A and B are shown. Door A has a recognisable card beneath it; Door B has an empty dashed frame. The answer labels have not appeared yet.

20.text:
Door A shows Mira the card.
Mira can look at it and point to it.

This card is an example.
20.subtext: An example is something shown for us to look at or check.
20.alt: Door A is labelled beside a card moving toward Mira. Written labels name CARD SHOWN, HANDOVER and MIRA LOOKING.

21.text:
Door B has not shown Mira a card.
We have not seen an object from Door B yet.
21.subtext: We can say: no example was given. We do not invent one.
21.alt: Door B is labelled beside an empty dashed frame. Written labels name NO CARD SHOWN YET, EMPTY FRAME and MIRA LOOKING; no secret object appears.

23.text:
Made a mark? The mark is here.
Made no mark? The card is still here.

Neither choice made nothing appear.
23.subtext: We could still point to the mark, the card or the choice.
23.alt: Two large cards are labelled MARK HERE and BLANK CARD HERE, keeping the present card distinct from the absent mark.

24.text:
Show something—and we have something to look at.
If no object is shown, we have no object from that door to use.
24.subtext: That is what no example was given means.
24.alt: Mira's detective board links a shown card to SOMETHING TO LOOK AT and an empty dashed frame to NOTHING SHOWN YET.

25.alt: An open brown treasure chest reveals a gold card reading THERE IS NO NOTHING. Mira and Pip stand beside five clue stars and a ticket reading BOOK CODE TWODOORS.

26.text:
Our game talks about what someone can show, say, draw or save in a note.

It does not guess about what no one has shown.
26.subtext: A careful detective says exactly what the game can check.
26.alt: A green game mat contains four recognisable symbols labelled SHOW, SAY, DRAW and SAVE IN A NOTE. Beyond its rope boundary is an unmarked area containing no invented object.

27.text:
Find four clues:
an empty box, a still bell, a blank card and a partly hidden toy.
27.subtext: For each clue, say what is here and what did not happen or appear.

28.text:
Box here—no toy inside.
Bell here—no ring.
Card here—no mark.
Curtain here—toy partly hidden.
28.subtext: You kept each missing thing separate from the things still here.
28.alt: The final search scene returns with words naming EMPTY BOX, STILL BELL, BLANK CARD, CURTAIN and TOY PARTLY HIDDEN. The teddy remains partly visible below the curtain.

29.text:
Which pictures show an object you can look at?
Which empty frame means: no object was shown yet?
29.subtext: Move your finger from each picture or frame to a basket.
29.alt: Three recognisable pictures show an empty box, a still bell and a blank card. A fourth position is an empty dashed frame. The two baskets are labelled OBJECT TO LOOK AT and NOTHING SHOWN YET.

30.text:
Box, bell and card: objects to look at.
Empty frame: no object was shown yet.
30.subtext: That is what NO EXAMPLE GIVEN means.
30.alt: Recognisable box, bell and blank-card pictures have green lines to OBJECT TO LOOK AT. The empty dashed frame has a purple line to NOTHING SHOWN YET.
